question.text: 'Yamuna Alpha Fund', a Category III open-ended AIF with NAV of INR 200 crore, is considering increasing its total long+short exposure to INR 450 crore. Under Regulation 18A prudential norms, what is the compliance position?

answer.text: Permissible — Cat III AIFs can leverage up to 3x NAV
Permissible — the leverage cap is on borrowings only, not total exposure
Permissible with investor consent beyond 2x, no absolute ceiling
Not permissible — leverage (total long + short, after offsetting) cannot exceed 2x NAV; INR 450 cr = 2.25x NAV

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular CIR/IMD/DF/10/2013 (operational/prudential norms) and Regulation 18A: Cat III leverage = (Total exposure: Long + Short after offsetting) / NAV must not exceed 2x. For NAV INR 200 cr, max exposure = INR 400 cr. INR 450 cr = 2.25x — breach. NAV excludes borrowings. The Trap: Option A cites a non-existent 3x cap. Option B ignores derivative exposure. Option C is plainly wrong — the 2x is a hard SEBI cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) directly tests 2x NAV. XIX-C requires the ratio formula and the breach-reporting timelines. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: On breach, report to custodian immediately; intimate ALL investors before 10:00 AM next working day; square-off excess by end of next working day; send square-off confirmation same day. Custodian reports breach to SEBI before 10:00 AM next working day. Build automated EOD leverage monitors to trigger these workflows.
